Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test method testAxisFollowing is testing XPath expressions involving the following::node() axis with namespaces. The bug report points to an issue in DOMNodePointer.java at line 120 (around testNode method) which implements node() matching logic in the DOM model.

Examining the testNode(Node, NodeTest) method:
- At line 146, when the NodeTest is of type NODE_TYPE_NODE (which corresponds to node()), it only returns true if the node is an ELEMENT_NODE or DOCUMENT_NODE.
- The bug report correctly points out that this is too restrictive: the node() test should match any node, not just element or document nodes.
- The correct behavior for node() is to return true for any node, therefore line 147-148 should change from return nodeType == ELEMENT_NODE || nodeType == DOCUMENT_NODE to simply return true.

This matches the bug report's suggestion:
```
case Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE:
    return true;
```

Because the testAxisFollowing is failing when trying to select following::node()[2], which might include any node (element, text, comment, etc.), the existing restrictive check causes nodes to be incorrectly excluded.

The other recent bug reports about ParentNullChecks or NodeSets do not relate to this node type matching issue.

In summary:
- The cause of failure is that the testNode method incorrectly filters node() XPath tests too restrictively to ELEMENT_NODE and DOCUMENT_NODE.
- The testAxisFollowing test requires the correct behavior that node() matches all node types.
- Fixing testNode to return true for NODE_TYPE_NODE case will correct this behavior.

This diagnosis matches the current bug report's pointer and the location of the relevant code.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
